title: Sort a Class with Venn Diagrams Explained Simply | PUC Maths Class 11
description:
Some classmates take Biology, some take Maths, a few take both, and one takes neither. Two lists repeat names and a table gets messy, but two circles inside a rectangle sort everyone at a glance. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Maths (NCERT Chapter 1, Sets) we learn to draw and read Venn diagrams, named after the English logician John Venn (1834-1923).

You will watch Diya's class sorted live into four regions and name each one in set language (B − M, B ∩ M, M − B, (B ∪ M)′), compare subset, disjoint and overlapping circles, see union, intersection, difference and complement shaded one after another, and count the eight regions of a three-set diagram. Then a worked example placing the numbers 1 to 10, the exam trap of forgetting the rectangle, an original JEE Main pattern question on a shaded three-set region with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11 and JEE Main students.

In this video:
0:00 Biology, Maths or both?
0:32 What a Venn diagram is (John Venn)
0:50 Live: sort the class into circles
1:19 Two circles, four regions
1:39 Subset, disjoint or overlapping
2:27 Live: shade union, intersection, difference, complement
2:47 Three sets: eight regions
3:16 Worked example: even numbers and multiples of 3
4:02 Exam trap: forgetting the rectangle
4:16 Where it is asked
4:27 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
5:00 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode (Ep 11): Properties of Set Operations. Does the order of union and intersection ever change the answer?
